name: Slack (OAuth v2 app install)
summary: Create a Slack app, add an HTTPS redirect URL and scopes, send users to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize, and exchange the code with oauth.v2.access. Installing outside your own workspace needs public distribution; commercial apps go through Slack Marketplace review. Generated live by the research agent from Slack's developer docs; nothing here was exercised in a Slack workspace.

active.basis: No hands-on run, so no effort figure is claimed.

wait.basis: Unlisted distribution is a dashboard button. Slack Marketplace listing involves a review, but the pages checked state no review duration.

prerequisites.text: A Slack workspace where you build the app. Until you enable distribution, the app installs only there.

source.quote: By default, a newly built Slack app can only be installed in its associated workspace as mentioned above.

prerequisites.text: Know your customers' policies: some workspaces only allow Marketplace-listed apps, so an unlisted app may be blocked there.

source.quote: Other workspaces may only allow the installation of apps officially listed in the Slack Marketplace.

steps.title: Create the app and find its client ID and secret
steps.detail: Create a Slack app in Slack's App Management pages. The client ID and client secret are listed there; keep the secret in your backend secret store.

source.quote: Include both your app's client ID, which is found in the App Management page, and a comma-separated list of scopes

steps.title: Add an HTTPS redirect URL
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions, add your agent application's callback. Plain http (including http://localhost) is not accepted, so local testing needs an HTTPS tunnel or certificate.

settings.explain: Illustrative production value. Any redirect_uri you send must match it or be a subdirectory of it, and cannot contain #.

steps.title: Choose bot scopes and, only if needed, user scopes
steps.detail: Bot scopes give your app its own identity; user scopes act as the installing user. Start with the minimum list.

source.quote: Bot scopes should be added as scope=<bot_scope> , and user scopes should be added as user_scope=<user_scope> .

steps.title: Expect scopes to accumulate across installs
steps.detail: Reinstalling with new scopes adds to the token; it never removes earlier ones. Removing a scope means revoking the token.

source.quote: There is no way to remove scopes from an existing token without revoking it entirely.

steps.title: Send the user to Slack's authorize URL
steps.detail: Link to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with client_id, scope and/or user_scope, redirect_uri and an unguessable state.

source.quote: To request scopes, redirect Slack users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize .

steps.title: Check state when the user returns
steps.detail: Slack adds a code (valid for ten minutes) to your redirect URL. Reject the request if state differs from what you stored.

source.quote: Check the state parameter if you sent one along with your initial user redirect.

steps.title: Exchange the code with oauth.v2.access
steps.detail: Send code, client_id, client_secret and the same redirect_uri you used to authorize. The response holds the bot token (and user token if requested).

source.quote: sends it to the oauth.v2.access API endpoint to exchange that code for an access token.

steps.title: Record which workspace or org was installed
steps.detail: The user can switch target during consent, so store team.id (or enterprise.id for org-level installs) from the response, not the value you asked for.

source.quote: The oauth.v2.access response is the source of truth

steps.title: Call the Web API with the token
steps.detail: Send Authorization: Bearer <token> on each request.

source.quote: The best way to communicate your access tokens — also known as bearer tokens — to Slack is by presenting them in a request's Authorization HTTP header

steps.title: Plan for token lifetime and revocation
steps.detail: Tokens do not expire unless you opt into token rotation. Revoke unneeded tokens with auth.revoke.

steps.title: Activate public distribution to install in other workspaces
steps.detail: App dashboard → Manage Distribution → Share Your App with Other Workspaces. This makes the app installable elsewhere without a Marketplace listing.

steps.title: For commercial launch, submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Marketplace listing is a separate approval from distribution. Review time is not stated on the pages checked.

source.quote: Unlike unlisted distributed apps, apps listed in the Slack Marketplace are reviewed against our requirements & guidelines to ensure a quality experience for end users.

gaps.text: Nothing was exercised in a Slack workspace; every step is documentation-backed only.
gaps.next_action: Create a test app in a sandbox workspace and run one install with a minimal bot scope.

gaps.text: Slack Marketplace review requirements and timeline were not researched.
gaps.next_action: Read the Slack Marketplace guide before planning a commercial launch date.

gaps.text: Slack's PKCE guide (listed in its docs navigation) was not read, so PKCE support details are not included.
gaps.next_action: Read docs.slack.dev 'Using PKCE' if your client cannot keep a secret.

verification.method: plain HTTPS fetch, tags stripped, normalized text match
